outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: Minor punctuation/label formatting (e.g., “Software Developers, 15-1252.00” vs header styling) would be inconsequential if all required values were provided.

Critical issues: The agent failed to provide several required deliverables: annual median wage, current employment, projected-growth wording and rate, and projected job openings. These are not optional; they are explicitly required and part of the task’s stopping condition. DOM evidence confirms the agent was on the correct O*NET summary page for 15-1252.00 and correctly captured the occupation title/code, Bright Outlook presence, and Job Zone title (visible in DOM states 0–2). However, across the final states provided, none of the national Wages & Employment Trends values were extracted, and there is no environment blocker indicated—only limited scrolling occurred and the agent ended by stating the values were not visible. From an average user perspective, the primary intent (recording all requested fields exactly as displayed) is not met because the key wage/employment/projection/openings fields—the main “data extraction” portion—are missing.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to read the O*NET OnLine Summary Report for Software Developers (occupation code 15-1252.00) and extract a specific set of fields (title/code, Bright Outlook, Job Zone title, and the national Wages & Employment Trends figures for annual median wage, current employment, projected growth wording+rate, and projected job openings), preserving exact displayed wording/formatting. A reasonable user would be flexible on minor formatting (commas/labels) but not flexible on missing any of the requested fields or using non-national/non-O*NET sources.
